data.one_liner: On-device ML inference for Flutter using PyTorch ExecuTorch and dart:ffi.
data.what_it_does: ExecuTorch Flutter provides a Dart API for loading and running ExecuTorch machine learning models (.pte files) and experimental streaming LLMs directly on-device. It handles native platform integration across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Web.
use_when: You need to run PyTorch machine learning models locally on mobile, desktop, or web.
You want support for streaming on-device LLMs or real-time camera inference.
avoid_when: You prefer running heavy inference on remote servers rather than on-device.
You are using BERT-family tokenizers (WordPiece) which are unsupported by the native tokenizer.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Web.
Supports multiple backends like XNNPACK, CoreML, Metal, and experimental Vulkan or MLX.
Includes experimental streaming text generation for on-device LLMs.
weaknesses: Requires platform configuration and native build hooks setup.
Tokenizers do not support WordPiece/BERT-family models.
Some backends like Vulkan or MLX are experimental or platform-restricted.
data.setup_notes: Requires native build configuration under pubspec.yaml hooks.user_defines, setting iOS/macOS deployment targets, and running setup_web for web targets.

alternatives.name: tflite_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you prefer TensorFlow Lite models over PyTorch ExecuTorch for on-device inference.

alternatives.name: llamadart
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose this if you want a dedicated Dart library for LLaMA model inference without the ExecuTorch dependency.
